1.
Heard Sri Ashish Verma, learned counsel for the petitioners as well as learned Standing Counsel for the respondents.

2. By means of present writ petition the petitioners have assailed charge sheet dated 17.06.2023,
issued by Tehsildar, Musafirkhana, District - Amethi as well as have sought direction to the respondents to withdraw the departmental proceedings initiated against the petitioners.

3. Brief facts giving rise to present writ petition are that the petitioners were appointed as Lekhpals on different dates and while performing their duties as Lekhpal of different villages in Tehsil - Musafirkhana, District - Amethi work of widening and constructions of National Highway No. 56 (Varanasi to Lucknow via Jaunpur, Sultanpur, Amethi) was initiated and for the said purposes a notification was issued under the National Highways Act, 1956 for acquisition of land.

As per guidelines of National Highways Authority a joint Inspection Committee was constituted to conduct spot inspection and go through the revenue records as there were number of villagers whose land had been acquired and number of awards had to be passed in the acquisition proceedings.

4. Prior to making of the awards, procedure as prescribed under the relevant Act was to be undertaken and the revenue officers including area Lekhpals were required to furnish relevant information on the basis of which valuation of land so acquired was to be determined by the competent authority.

Subsequently, under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Uttar Pradesh) Act, 2013,

It is for the said purposes that charge sheets were given to the petitioners on 17.06.2023, which has been assailed in the present writ petitions.

5. It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that charges levelled in the charge sheet are vague and also that the documents which are to be sought to be relied upon by the respondents in support of the charges, have not been provided to the petitioners and it is on these two grounds that in the present writ petitions prayer has been made to quash the charge sheets and also to set aside the departmental proceedings.
6. This Court has perused the order sheet of this Court wherein it is found that directions were issued by this Court to the respondents to provide documents to the petitioners within specified time.

It is the contention of the petitioners that despite directions issued by this Court the respondents have not handed over all the documents and due to which the petitioners are unable to file their reply and due to this fact the departmental proceedings are pending.
7. Learned Standing Counsel on the other hand has opposed the writ petition.
He has submitted that perusal of charge sheet would indicate that specific charges have been levelled against petitioners and details of which are given in the charge sheet itself.

Further he submits that in case any particular document is required or any record is sought to be inspected then it is open for the petitioners to move appropriate application before the inquiry officer, who on receipt of such application shall pass appropriate orders thereupon.

It is open for the petitioners to submits their reply and participate in the departmental proceedings while on the other hand the departmental authorities are required to conclude the said proceedings with expedition in accordance with law.

8. Learned Standing Counsel submits that it is needless to say that in case there is any infirmity in the departmental proceedings, then it is open for the delinquent employee to challenge the order passed in the departmental proceedings either in appeal or before the appropriate authority, but this Court in exercise of power under Article 226 of the Constitution of India would not monitor the departmental proceedings and prays for dismissal of writ petitions.

9. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
10.

Challenge in the present case has been made to the charge sheet dated 17.03.2023, wherein three charges have been leveled against petitioners while they were discharging their duties as Lekhpals at different Villages of Tehsil - Musafirkhana, District - Amethi.

In the first charge allegation is that the petitioners failed to correctly provide the distance of the main highway from the land acquired thereby directly effecting the valution of the land, due to which higher compensation was paid to the farmers.

Five documents have been indicated to be relied upon by the respondents in support of charges levelled against the petitioners in the said inquiry and in ordinary course all the five documents should have been provided alongwith the charge sheet to the delinquent employee.

sentences.text:
In charge no. 2 specifically pertains to the acquisition of land between 100 to 113.600 Kms. from National Highway 56 and the allegation relates to higher compensation paid to the farmers then what should have been awarded to the farmers in lieu of their acquired land.
12.

This Court finds that specific charge has been levelled against petitioners where distance of the land from the National Highway which was sought to be acquired has also been given and quantum of compensation which was awarded on higher side has also been provided.
Again there are five documents which have been relied upon in support of charge have also been given therein.
This Court is of the considered view that once charges are very clear in their terms then there is no occasion for assailing the same on the ground that they are vague.

It may be possible that documents sought by the petitioners have not been given to them, and grievance raised in this regard shall be raised before the disciplinary authority and not in the writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
The disciplinary authority on the other hand is bound to give all the documents reliance upon which has been placed by the prosecution in support of charges.

13. Rules of 1999 clearly provide for a time bound inquiry and accordingly time for giving reply is also provided for in the charge sheet and time may be enlarged on the request made by delinquent employee, clearly stating the reasons for enlargement of time for giving reply.

Such extension cannot be given for indefinite period of time and accordingly even if the documents are not provided, it is open for the delinquent employee to submit his reply in absence of relevant documents and thereafter the inquiry officer shall proceed in terms of Rules, 1999 and conclude the proceedings in accordance with law as per provisions laid down therein.
14.

This Court does not find any reason to keep the present writ petition pending as there is no infirmity in the charge sheet and charges are extremely specific relating to alleged misconduct on behalf of petitioners.
15. Accordingly, for the reasons aforesaid, present writ petition being bereft of merits is dismissed.

16. The disciplinary authority is directed to see that the directions given by this Court are complied with and the disciplinary proceedings initiated against the petitioners is concluded with expedition.
